correctness.rationale: An independent interval-feasibility proof avoids assuming the location of the quadratic extremum. Write w(z)=z(z−1). Tolerance M at z imposes θ ∈ [1/z−M/w(z), 1/z+M/w(z)]. These closed intervals have common intersection iff the lower bound at u is at most the upper bound at v for all u<v (the reverse order imposes no positive constraint). Thus the optimum is the maximum of (1/u−1/v)/(1/w(u)+1/w(v)). Both the positive numerator and the reciprocal of the denominator increase with v, so take v=y. With a=u−1 and b=y−1 the ratio is ab(b−a)/(a(a+1)+b(b+1)). Its derivative in a has the sign of b²−2ab−a², hence its maximum on [x−1,b] is at a=max{x−1,(√2−1)b}. The active pair pins θ uniquely at their coincident interval boundaries; equivalently θ=((u−1)+(y−1))/(w(u)+w(y)), which lies strictly between 1/y and 1/u≤1/x. Substitution gives both frozen formulas, the branch join, and θ<1/2. In the interior branch the inequality M≤1 is d²≤1+2d, equivalent to y≤4+2√2. At fixed width Δ the endpoint branch is eventually active and division by y² yields Δ/2. On [0,2] both factors have magnitude at most one; the spectral theorem then gives the stated Euclidean norm result.
residual_risks: The cutoff applies only to the first branch, not to all bands. Interval-robust exact-arithmetic SPD result, not a nonnormal, finite-precision or finite-spectrum optimality guarantee.

value.rationale: Prescribing the large step models the already committed unstable update in explicit stabilization. The exact optimum replaces single-frequency sufficiency with robust tuning under band uncertainty, identifies the lower-edge-independent branch, and separates the sharp wide-band cutoff from narrow-band rescue at arbitrarily high frequencies. It gives a usable step and operator norm, not merely a numerical improvement.
residual_risks: No floating-point stability, accuracy-versus-cost, or performance claim for nonlinear or nonnormal systems.
